title: A lower heat capacity
hook: Transfer heat and watch the thermometer respond.

doesNotKnow: How mass and specific heat determine the change for a given heat transfer.

misconception: The same heat always produces the same temperature change regardless of mass or material.
objective: Apply q = mcΔT under the stated ideal assumptions.

claims.text: Question, model and explanation: A model block has mass 10 g and constant specific heat 1 J/(g·°C). It begins at 20 °C and receives 40 J as heat. With no phase change or other energy transfer, what is its final temperature? Using q = mcΔT, ΔT = 40/(10 × 1) = 4 °C. Starting at 20 °C gives 24 °C. This is an ideal block with constant specific heat.
The block and thermometer are schematic; the numerical values describe an idealized model, not a named material.

Recall: If mass and specific heat stay fixed, what happens to the magnitude of ΔT when the magnitude of heat transfer doubles? From q = mcΔT, the temperature change is proportional to heat when m and c stay fixed.
For a fixed mass and specific heat, a larger magnitude of heat transfer produces a larger temperature change.

recall.question: If mass and specific heat stay fixed, what happens to the magnitude of ΔT when the magnitude of heat transfer doubles?
recall.why: From q = mcΔT, the temperature change is proportional to heat when m and c stay fixed.
